name: Xcel Energy
description: Xcel Energy is a regulated electric and natural gas delivery company serving about 3.9 million electric and 2.2 million gas customers in eight states (Minnesota, Colorado, Texas, New Mexico, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota) through four operating utilities. It earns money by building power plants, wires and gas pipes that state regulators add to a rate base on which it is allowed a set return. Regulated electric is about 83 percent of revenue and 88 percent of utility net income. The story of the last two years is wildfire liability: settlements for the 2021 Marshall Fire (PSCo, $640 million) and the 2024 Smokehouse Creek fire (SPS), which hit Colorado's earned return (5.66 percent GAAP ROE in 2025 against authorised returns of about 9 to 10 percent in the rate cases cited).

gics.note: Wikipedia list gives only sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry were not in a source read, so left null.

hq.note: 414 Nicollet Mall, Minneapolis, MN 55401; incorporated in Minnesota in 1909 (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Regulated electric
businessLines.how: Customers pay regulated retail rates and riders; Xcel recovers fuel costs and earns an allowed ROE (equity ratios 52.5% to 56%) on the rate base it invests in, so profit rises with approved capital spending.
businessLines.description: Electric generation, transmission and distribution by NSP-Minnesota, NSP-Wisconsin, PSCo and SPS

businessLines.name: Regulated natural gas
businessLines.how: Regulated delivery charges per customer and per therm plus a pass-through of gas costs; earns an allowed ROE on gas pipe and storage rate base.
businessLines.description: Natural gas distribution, transportation and storage (NSP-Minnesota, NSP-Wisconsin, PSCo; WGI and WYCO pipelines)

whatsNext.text: Colorado electric rate case filed Nov 2025 seeking +$356M (9.9%), 9.8% ROE, 55% equity ratio; Colorado gas case +$190M, rate base $4.7B; Minnesota electric case (10.3% ROE, $13.2B rate base 2025) pending; New Mexico electric case +$175M filed Nov 2025
Texas Attorney General lawsuit against SPS over Smokehouse Creek Fire (filed Dec 2025) unresolved; remaining SPS claims unsettled
